newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower on exports, weather.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower on exports, weather.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed lower, weakened by a combination of bearish export data, good spring wheat plantings weather and crop boosting rains in Kansas, floor sources said.
"The export inspections this morning were disappointing and we are also making good progress planting spring wheat," a dealer said.

USDA's weekly planting progress report, to be issued later Monday, was expected to show spring wheat 75 to 80 percent planted, up from 59 percent a week earlier. Winter wheat in Kansas also received needed rain over the holiday weekend.
USDA said for the week ended May 22 U.S. wheat inspected for export totaled 6.960 million bushels, below expectations for 10 million to 14 million bushels.

Featured sellers included Benson Quinn (2.5 million bushels July, 500,000 bushels September), Prudential Securities (1.0 million July, 700,000 December) and Country Hedging (800,000 July, 700,000 September).
Buyers included Atwood-Peavy (1.4 million July, 1.0 million December).
July closed down 12-1/4 cents at $3.81-3/4 a bushel, with other months 10 to six cents lower.
